Generative policies offer expressive action distributions
for online reinforcement learning (RL).
Diffusion- and flow-based policies can capture multimodal
distributions that are difficult to represent with a single
Gaussian
(
Dong et al., 2025
;
Celik et al., 2025
)
.
However, many of these approaches generate actions through
iterative sampling, requiring repeated network evaluations
during training and inference.
Recent MeanFlow-based methods reduce this cost through
few-step or one-step action generation
(
Dong et al., 2026
;
Chen et al., 2025
;
Kim et al., 2026
)
.
Drifting offers a different way to train one-step
generators
(
Deng et al., 2026
)
.
At each training iteration, it uses target data to
move generated samples toward the desired distribution,
then trains the generator to reproduce the moved
samples from the same inputs.
Through these repeated updates, the generator learns
to produce samples from the target distribution in
a single forward pass at inference.
This approach has shown better performance than
MeanFlow variants in one-step image generation on
ImageNet
(
Deng et al., 2026
)
.
These results motivate exploring Drifting for online
RL, where its use remains less studied.
We consider the maximum-entropy (MaxEnt) RL objective,
which balances expected return with policy entropy
to encourage exploration
(
Haarnoja et al., 2018
)
.
The critic defines a Boltzmann target distribution
for policy improvement, but does not directly provide
samples from it
(
Li et al., 2026
)
.
We therefore adopt an energy-based view of Drifting
(
Gretton et al., 2026
;
Han et al., 2026
)
,
using the negative MaxEnt policy-improvement objective
as the energy.
This energy guides updates to actions generated by
the current policy.
For the value term, critic gradients tell us how to
move actions toward higher values.
The entropy term is harder to use: an implicit actor
generates actions but does not provide a tractable
density for computing their distribution’s entropy.
We therefore need training targets that capture
the effect of entropy without explicitly computing it.
We propose
DriftSpread
, a one-step generative policy in the
Drifting model family for online MaxEnt RL.
Our key idea is to derive two updates from this energy
and fit them sequentially to the same actor through
repeated Drift–Spread cycles.
In each cycle, Drift uses critic gradients to move
generated actions toward higher values.
The actor then learns to reproduce these updated
actions from the same inputs through regression.
Spread captures the entropy contribution through
diffusion of the action distribution.
We approximate this diffusion by adding appropriately
scaled independent noise to actions from the updated
actor, then train the actor to match the resulting
distribution.
This allows the actor to learn the effect of entropy
without explicitly computing it.
For a fixed critic, we prove
that the learned policy converges to the Boltzmann
target distribution in the small-step, long-time limit.
Our main contributions are:
(1) We introduce
DriftSpread
, a Drifting model for online
MaxEnt RL with expressive policies and one-step action
generation.
(2) We develop sequential Drift–Spread training through
critic-guided regression and entropy regularization to
address the challenge of entropy computation for implicit
policies.
(3) On MuJoCo,
DriftSpread
outperforms 13 baselines
in aggregate normalized return, with lower training
costs than the diffusion, flow, and MeanFlow baselines
(Figure
1
).

Related Work
Generative policies for online RL.
Diffusion and flow models provide expressive action
distributions for online RL.
One line of work optimizes policies by backpropagating
critic gradients through diffusion or flow sampling
(
Wang et al., 2024
;
Lyu et al., 2025
)
.
DIME also differentiates through diffusion sampling
while optimizing a variational lower bound on the
MaxEnt objective
(
Celik et al., 2025
)
.
Another line of work constructs training targets
for learning critic-defined Boltzmann distributions.
DQS uses weighted averages of critic gradients
to construct score targets
(
Jain et al., 2025
)
.
SDAC and MaxEntDP instead use critic values to weight
denoising supervision and noise estimates, respectively
(
Ma et al., 2025
;
Dong et al., 2025
)
.
Reverse flow matching unifies these gradient-expectation
and noise-expectation formulations through posterior-mean
estimation
(
Li et al., 2026
)
.
These approaches use iterative action sampling,
motivating few-step and one-step policies for online RL.
MeanFlow was introduced for one-step generative modeling
and learns average velocities
(
Geng et al., 2025
)
.
Recent online RL methods use this formulation
to learn policies with fewer generation steps.
FPMD trains rectified-flow and MeanFlow policies
through policy mirror descent, with both variants
supporting one-step inference
(
Chen et al., 2025
)
.
MFPO trains few-step MeanFlow policies using velocity
estimates for critic-defined Boltzmann targets
(
Dong et al., 2026
)
, while SOM constructs velocity
targets from critic-based score estimates to train
one-step MeanFlow policies
(
Kim et al., 2026
)
.
Drifting models and policy learning.
Drifting learns one-step generators by repeatedly
moving generated samples and training the generator
to reproduce their updated positions.
This approach has achieved state-of-the-art performance
in one-step image generation on ImageNet
(
Deng et al., 2026
)
.
Subsequent work relates specific Drifting fields
to Wasserstein gradient flows
(
Gretton et al., 2026
)
and uses
optimal-transport couplings to construct sample
updates
(
He et al., 2026
)
.
W-Flow derives sample movements from an objective
over distributions and trains a one-step generator
on the resulting samples
(
Han et al., 2026
)
.
Drifting has also been applied to policy learning.
For offline RL, DriftQL combines critic-guided
policy improvement with a Drifting regularizer
based on the behavior distribution
(
Houssaini et al., 2026
)
.
For offline-to-online RL, Drifting Field Policy
derives a KL-regularized policy update through
Wasserstein gradient flow and constructs training
targets from actions ranked by the critic
(
Koo et al., 2026
)
.
Our work focuses on online MaxEnt RL from scratch.

6
Conclusion and Limitations
We introduced
DriftSpread
, a Drifting-based approach to
learning expressive one-step policies for online RL.
Building on an energy-based view of Drifting, we derive
critic-guided Drift and entropy-induced Spread from
the MaxEnt objective.
The two updates are learned sequentially by the same
actor: Drift moves actions toward higher values,
while Spread matches a broader distribution constructed
from the updated actor.
This design incorporates the effect of entropy without
estimating policy densities or scores, while allowing
each action sample to be generated in one forward pass.
Under exact fitting, our analysis establishes convergence
to the fixed-critic Boltzmann target in the small-step,
long-time limit.
MuJoCo experiments show that
DriftSpread
combines strong
control performance with efficient training and inference,
supporting Drifting as a practical approach to
generative policy learning.
Our work leaves two directions for future research.
First, our evaluation is limited to simulation
environments.
Testing on real-world control tasks would help
assess robustness to observation noise and changes
in system dynamics.
Second, we use a fixed spreading-noise distribution
and scale during training.
Adapting the spreading strength as learning progresses
may better balance exploration and value improvement.

article.headline: 漂移再扩散：一步生成策略新方法
article.lede: DriftSpread 用 critic 梯度做漂移、就势加噪做扩散，顺序训练同一 actor 的一步生成策略。
article.problem: 扩散与流匹配策略能给在线强化学习带来表达能力强的动作分布，但往往需要多步迭代采样，训练和推理代价都高，MeanFlow 等少步方法只缓解了部分成本。Drifting 为一步生成提供了另一条训练路径，已在 ImageNet 上优于 MeanFlow 变体，但在在线 RL 中尚未充分研究。在线最大熵 RL 要求策略逼近 critic 定义的 Boltzmann 分布，而该目标只以能量形式给出、无法直接采样，隐式 actor 也拿不出可处理的密度或 score 来计算熵项。
article.method: DriftSpread 从负 MaxEnt 目标出发，借助 Wasserstein 梯度流把策略演化拆成两项：由 critic 梯度引导的 Drift 和由熵诱导的 Spread。训练时在同一 actor 上顺序执行：先用动作回归拟合 a+η∇Q 的停止梯度目标，再对更新后的动作加入协方差为 2ληI 的独立噪声，并用基于特征函数、无需密度估计的 MMD 匹配这一分布。在精确拟合、critic 固定等假设下，论文证明步长趋于零、演化时间趋于无穷时策略弱收敛到 Boltzmann 目标。
article.results: 在 MuJoCo 五个任务、每任务 100 万次环境交互、五个随机种子的设置下，DriftSpread 的聚合归一化回报在全部 13 个基线中最高，但论文未给出该聚合值的具体数值。单步推理耗时为每动作 0.15 ms，低于 DIME 的 1.24 ms 与两步 MeanFlow 策略 MFPO 的 0.36 ms；HalfCheetah-v3 与 Walker2d-v3 上晚期平均回报排名第一。二维高斯 Boltzmann 示例中，顺序拟合的最终 KL 为 0.000422，网格搜索权重后的联合拟合为 0.512165，后者方差比约 (0.80, 3.15)，一维过窄、另一维过宽。
article.why_it_matters: 在线 RL 的生成式策略长期在表达力与采样成本之间取舍，一步前向生成动作意味着多模态动作分布可以进入对控制频率敏感的场景。该方法也给出了一条工程化路径：不依赖隐式策略的密度与 score 估计，而是通过加噪与分布匹配来体现熵项的作用。
article.limitations: 评测只覆盖 MuJoCo 仿真，未检验真实控制任务中的观测噪声与动力学变化；收敛性分析以精确拟合和固定 critic 为前提，与在线训练的实际过程存在差距。扩散噪声的分布与尺度在训练中固定，频率尺度等超参对结果敏感，论文附录显示偏离默认尺度会变差，而且每个任务单独设定 Spread 学习率也增加了调参负担。
article.figure_caption_zh: DriftSpread 总览：(a) 训练在 critic 学习与顺序 Drift–Spread actor 更新之间交替，Drift 用动作回归、Spread 用分布匹配；(b) 曲面示意负 MaxEnt 目标，样本显示 Drift 把动作推向更高 critic 值、Spread 再拓宽分布以体现熵。

page_papers.title: Prospective Forcing: Learning to Look Ahead for Autoregressive Long Video Diffusion
page_papers.abstract: Autoregressive video generators synthesize long videos through chunk-wise rollouts, yet they are typically trained to predict only the immediate future. This limited prediction horizon makes it challenging to maintain video quality over extended rollouts. To address this problem, we introduce Prospective Forcing, a multi-head prediction framework that injects long-range predictive signals into autoregressive video representations. Built on a rolling-window generator, Prospective Forcing attaches lightweight, offset-specific heads that share the same conditioning information and independently predict chunks at different future temporal offsets. By extending supervision beyond the next chunk, these heads encourage the shared history representation to retain information useful for longer-horizon prediction, supporting temporally consistent generation. At inference time, we accelerate sampling by using accepted future-chunk predictions to skip full-window backbone executions. We equip the head with learnable embeddings to generate multiple candidates for the next chunk, and a learned verifier either selects a candidate or rejects all and falls back to standard autoregressive generation.
page_papers.content:
Prospective Forcing: Learning to Look Ahead for Autoregressive Long Video Diffusion
Yifan Shen  Yewei Xia  Gongxu Luo  Peiyuan Zhu  Boyang Sun
Affiliation:
Mohamed bin Zayed University of AI   Carnegie Mellon University   Institute of Foundation Models
Zhenhao Chen  Guangyi Liu  Guangyi Chen  Kun Zhang
Affiliation:
Mohamed bin Zayed University of AI   Carnegie Mellon University   Institute of Foundation Models
Abstract
Autoregressive video generators synthesize long videos through chunk-wise rollouts, yet they are typically trained to predict only the immediate future. This limited prediction horizon makes it challenging to maintain video quality over extended rollouts. To address this problem, we introduce Prospective Forcing, a multi-head prediction framework that injects long-range predictive signals into autoregressive video representations. Built on a rolling-window generator, Prospective Forcing attaches lightweight, offset-specific heads that share the same conditioning information and independently predict chunks at different future temporal offsets. By extending supervision beyond the next chunk, these heads encourage the shared history representation to retain information useful for longer-horizon prediction, supporting temporally consistent generation. At inference time, we accelerate sampling by using accepted future-chunk predictions to skip full-window backbone executions. We equip the head with learnable embeddings to generate multiple candidates for the next chunk, and a learned verifier either selects a candidate or rejects all and falls back to standard autoregressive generation.

†

†

Figure 1:
By learning to predict future, Prospective Forcing generates long videos that remain dynamic, temporally consistent, and visually stable from a single text prompt.
1
Introduction
“The future enters into us, in order to transform itself in us,
long before it happens.”
— Rainer Maria Rilke,
Letters to a Young Poet
Autoregressive video generation provides a natural framework for modeling dynamic visual worlds by extending a video one chunk at a time, which supports generative interactive environments
(
Bruce et al., 2024
)
, real-time game simulation
(
Valevski et al., 2025
)
, robot control
(
Li et al., 2026
)
, and other applications that require coherent long-term visual rollouts. However, maintaining temporal consistency over long videos remains an open challenge. A rollout may remain locally plausible while subject identity, background appearance, spatial layout, color, and object structure gradually drift. These failures become more visible as the generation proceeds. This drift stems from a lack of long-horizon predictive capability, as next-chunk supervision prioritizes immediate continuation without requiring representations to preserve the information needed to anticipate more distant futures. We refer to this myopic behavior as
temporal shortsightedness
.
Existing approaches improve the temporal consistency from different perspectives. Conditioning the model on self-generated histories during training makes later predictions more robust to an imperfectly generated context
(
Huang et al., 2025a
)
. Rolling-window generation jointly denoises adjacent chunks with progressive noise levels and retains initial states as global anchors, reducing error accumulation while preserving a reference to the beginning of the video
(
Liu et al., 2026
)
. Training-free methods extend pretrained video generators by rescheduling noise across overlapping temporal windows or maintaining a queue of partially denoised frames
(
Qiu et al., 2024
;
Kim et al., 2024
)
. Other approaches combine short-term conditioning on features from the preceding chunk with long-term preservation of scene and object features from the initial chunk
(
Henschel et al., 2025
)
.
These approaches primarily address exposure bias, inference-time context preservation, or temporal denoising schedules. We introduce Prospective Forcing to address temporal shortsightedness through a complementary training objective. Specifically, the backbone encodes preceding chunks into a shared history representation, and independent heads combine it with target-specific diffusion noise to predict chunks at distinct future offsets. We train these heads through cross-chunk self-distillation using the backbone’s own subsequent outputs as the teacher. When a target chunk is reached later in the same causal rollout, the backbone’s detached feature and velocity predictions supervise the corresponding longer-offset prediction from an earlier context. These losses propagate through both the heads and the backbone, encouraging the shared representation to retain information needed across multiple future chunks. The resulting representation captures rapid changes in local motion while preserving relatively stable properties such as object identity and scene structure, consistent with the fast-and-slow perspective of hierarchical causal representation learning
(
Li et al., 2025
)
. We call it a
speculative representation
to reflect its long-term predictive capability. Section
5
further analyzes this representation in an idealized setting.
At inference, our default configuration uses the speculative representation to produce multiple candidate continuations. A lightweight learned verifier selects one candidate or rejects them all, in which case generation falls back to the standard autoregressive path. Each accepted candidate extends the video by one additional chunk without another sequential execution of the backbone, reducing the sampling cost. We evaluate on 30-second video generation with multiple metrics, where Prospective Forcing improves video quality, while accelerating sampling. Notably, the improvements persist even when the prediction heads are removed at inference, indicating that the speculative representation itself captures information that benefits long-horizon generation.
Our main contributions are as follows. First, we introduce Prospective Forcing to address temporal shortsightedness by learning a speculative representation that supports explicit prediction of multiple future chunks from the current state, thereby improving long-term video quality. Second, we develop a verifier-guided speculative inference procedure that reuses the prediction heads to extend rollouts without additional sequential backbone executions. Third, we demonstrate improved video quality across multiple video generation metrics alongside sampling speedups.

Related Work
Autoregressive video generation.
Unlike bidirectional video diffusion models which jointly denoise a fixed temporal window
(
Blattmann et al., 2023
;
Yang et al., 2025
;
Kong et al., 2024
;
Wan et al., 2025
)
, autoregressive models generate frames or chunks sequentially, enabling low-latency streaming with KV caching. Existing methods differ mainly in how the causal generator is trained: with per-token noise levels
(
Chen et al., 2024a
)
, by distilling few-step causal students from bidirectional or causal teachers via distribution matching
(
Yin et al., 2024
;
Yin et al., 2025
;
Huang et al., 2025a
;
Zhu et al., 2026
;
Zhao et al., 2026
)
, or end-to-end without a teacher
(
Guo et al., 2025
)
.
Long video generation.
To mitigate drift over long rollouts, prior methods either align training with long-horizon inference
(
Cui et al., 2026b
;
Yang et al., 2026
;
Chen et al., 2026
;
Lin et al., 2026
)
, design denoising schedules and anchor frames that preserve early context
(
Liu et al., 2026
;
Henschel et al., 2025
)
, or manage the KV cache and positional encoding at inference time without additional training
(
Yi et al., 2026
;
Cui et al., 2026a
)
. Instead, our method improves long video generation by learning representations with long-horizon predictive capabilities.
Future-predictive representations.
Predicting future observations has long served as an auxiliary objective for learning sequential representations in reinforcement learning
(
Guo et al., 2020
;
Schwarzer et al., 2021
)
, image generation
(
Yu et al., 2026b
)
, language modeling and speculative decoding
(
Gloeckle et al., 2024
;
Li et al., 2024
;
Cai et al., 2024
)
. Concurrent video works such as Video-Mirai
(
Yu et al., 2026a
)
and Next Forcing
(
Xu et al., 2026
)
incorporate future information via JEPA-style representation alignment
(
Bardes et al., 2024
)
and recurrent future-chunk prediction, respectively. In contrast, Prospective Forcing learns a shared representation for parallel multi-chunk prediction with independent heads, and reuses these heads for verifier-guided speculative inference. A more detailed discussion is provided in Appendix
B
.

Speculative inference.
In standard rolling inference, each backbone evaluation advances the window by only one chunk. A new chunk enters the last position as pure noise and must be processed once by the backbone before it can move forward. Design choices.
Table
4

We report the VBench Quality score together with three of its dimensions (subject consistency, dynamic degree, and imaging quality), and the MUSIQ drift. We first examine the architecture of the prediction heads. Sharing one head recursively across offsets, or using separate heads that each take the previous prediction as input, both underperform our parallel heads. We then vary what the heads read and predict. Feeding them more past chunks makes the prediction harder to learn and lowers quality, whereas supervising more positions of the future window raises the scores but collapses the dynamic degree and produces nearly static videos. Mapping the current chunk to a single future chunk therefore works best.
For the loss, training the same ODE-initialized model with DMD only, which is equivalent to Rolling Forcing, yields lower quality and substantially higher drift, showing that the gain comes from future alignment rather than initialization.
Removing the feature alignment loss degrades performance even below this DMD-only model, which indicates that learning the representation itself is essential. Finally, causal consistency distillation
(
Zhao et al., 2026
)
further improves over ODE
(
Yin et al., 2025
)
, showing that our method is complementary to a stronger initialization.
7
Conclusion
We introduced Prospective Forcing to address temporal shortsightedness in autoregressive long video diffusion. Rather than supervising only the next chunk, it trains lightweight heads to anticipate chunks at multiple future offsets, distilling targets from the backbone’s own later predictions. This turns the shared history into a speculative representation that looks beyond the immediate future. The same heads further enable verifier-guided speculative inference, which skips backbone executions whenever a predicted chunk is accepted and otherwise falls back to standard generation. Prospective Forcing outperforms baselines across multiple quantitative metrics and is preferred in human evaluations, while also achieving faster sampling.
Limitations.
Although Prospective Forcing accelerates sampling, the inference process still requires additional cache-update passes, which limits the speedup. We leave reducing this overhead to future work.

Appendix B
Related Work
Autoregressive video generation.
Modern video diffusion models typically denoise all frames in a fixed temporal window with bidirectional attention
(
Blattmann et al., 2023
;
Yang et al., 2025
;
Kong et al., 2024
;
Wan et al., 2025
)
. This design supports high-quality offline synthesis but requires the complete clip to be generated jointly. Autoregressive video models instead generate frames or chunks sequentially. This causal formulation reduces viewing latency and enables efficient streaming over extended horizons through KV caching
(
Yin et al., 2025
;
Huang et al., 2025a
)
. Within this family, Diffusion Forcing
(
Chen et al., 2024a
)
assigns an independent noise level to each token. It connects causal next-token prediction with full-sequence diffusion and supports flexible generation horizons. Another line uses distribution matching distillation (DMD)
(
Yin et al., 2024
)
to reduce the sampling cost of causal generators. CausVid
(
Yin et al., 2025
)
combines ODE initialization with asymmetric DMD to obtain a few-step causal student for real-time generation. Self Forcing
(
Huang et al., 2025a
)
trains on self-generated rollouts and applies a holistic distribution-matching objective to mitigate exposure bias. Causal Forcing
(
Zhu et al., 2026
)
uses an autoregressive ODE teacher to bridge the architectural gap between bidirectional teachers and causal students. Causal Forcing++
(
Zhao et al., 2026
)
replaces costly offline ODE trajectories with causal consistency distillation, making few-step initialization scalable. Beyond DMD-based post-training, Resampling Forcing
(
Guo et al., 2025
)
uses self-resampled histories and a sparse causal mask for teacher-free end-to-end training.
Long video generation.
Consistency over long autoregressive rollouts has been addressed through training, denoising, and context-management strategies. Self-Forcing++
(
Cui et al., 2026b
)
mitigates quality degradation when the student extrapolates beyond its training horizon by providing teacher guidance on segments sampled from self-generated long videos. Rolling Forcing
(
Liu et al., 2026
)
mitigates error accumulation by jointly denoising frames at progressively increasing noise levels within a rolling window and retaining initial-frame KV states as a global context anchor. StreamingT2V
(
Henschel et al., 2025
)
uses features from the preceding chunk to facilitate smooth transitions and preserves scene and object features from the first video chunk to prevent forgetting of the initial scene. LongLive
(
Yang et al., 2026
)
uses streaming long tuning to align long-video training and inference, together with short window attention and a frame sink to improve efficiency while preserving long-range consistency. Context Forcing
(
Chen et al., 2026
)
resolves the mismatch between a long-context student and a short-context teacher by training with a long-context teacher, while its Slow-Fast Memory architecture makes the growing context computationally tractable. DynaMem
(
Lin et al., 2026
)
addresses semantic drift, motion decay, and appearance instability through Semantic-Adaptive Hierarchical Memory, Motion-Prioritized Optimization, and Reference-Anchored Perceptual Alignment. Recent training-free approaches such as Deep Forcing and LoL implement context management at inference time by modifying cache retention and/or positional encoding. Deep Forcing
(
Yi et al., 2026
)
introduces Deep Sink, which retains a substantially enlarged attention sink with temporal RoPE adjustment, and Participative Compression, which prunes redundant and degraded history from the KV cache. LoL
(
Cui et al., 2026a
)
introduces multi-head RoPE jitter to break inter-head attention homogenization and mitigate sink-collapse over extreme horizons. Instead, our method improves temporal consistency by learning representations with long-horizon predictive capabilities.
Future-predictive representations and multi-horizon generation.
Predicting future observations has long served as an auxiliary supervision for learning sequential representations. PBL
(
Guo et al., 2020
)
couples forward prediction of future-observation embeddings with reverse prediction of agent states from the corresponding latents, achieving a bootstrapping objective. SPR
(
Schwarzer et al., 2021
)
instead rolls a learned transition model forward in latent space and matches its multi-step predictions to representations produced by an exponential-moving-average target encoder. In text generation, multi-token prediction
(
Gloeckle et al., 2024
)
equips a shared language-model trunk with independent output heads for predicting multiple subsequent tokens, while Medusa
(
Cai et al., 2024
)
and EAGLE
(
Li et al., 2024
)
accelerate LLM decoding by drafting future tokens with lightweight heads and verifying them against the backbone. In image generation, Mirai
(
Yu et al., 2026b
)
aligns internal representations with explicit or implicit foresight during autoregressive training while preserving the causal autoregressive inference path. The closest concurrent works in video generation are Video-Mirai and Next Forcing. Video-Mirai
(
Yu et al., 2026a
)
incorporates future information through alignment of JEPA-style representation
(
Bardes et al., 2024
)
, while Next Forcing
(
Xu et al., 2026
)
uses recurrent future chunk prediction to improve performance in robotic tasks. In contrast, Prospective Forcing learns a shared representation for parallel multi-chunk prediction through independent heads and reuses these heads for verifier-guided speculative inference.

D.3
Efficiency Measurement
We measure all methods on the same NVIDIA A100 80GB GPU with batch size one and bfloat16 precision. Table
5
breaks down the per-video inference cost. Generating a 30-second video involves two kinds of backbone passes: sampling passes that denoise the rolling window, and cache-update passes that write the key–value states of each newly committed clean chunk into the cache. article.headline: 让自回归视频生成提前预测更远的块
article.lede: Prospective Forcing 在滚动窗口生成器上加多个轻量预测头，并行预测未来第 1、2 个视频块，用跨块自蒸
article.problem: 自回归视频生成逐块推进，但训练目标只监督紧邻的下一个块，模型因此表现出「时间短视」：在长时间 rollout 中，主体身份、背景、布局和颜色会逐渐漂移。已有的曝光偏差修正、推理期上下文保持和去噪调度方法，都没有直接要求模型表示携带预测远期所需的信息。
article.method: 在滚动窗口里联合去噪 W=5 个块，取窗口最后一块的骨干特征，接 K=2 个轻量预测头并行预测后续第 1、2 块的特征与速度；监督信号来自同一因果 rollout 中后续窗口骨干自己的输出，并用 stop-gradient 做跨块自蒸馏。第一个头配有可学习的候选嵌入，可生成 M=2 个候选；一个轻量 MLP 验证器从中选一个，或全部拒绝并回退到标准自回归路径。当预测被接受时，该块直接提交，省去一次整窗骨干执行。
article.results: 在 200 条 MovieGen 提示词、30 秒 832×480/16fps 的设定下，方法取得 VBench Total 81.40、Quality 82.71、VBench-Long Quality 83.71、MUSIQ 69.14、漂移 3.64、FPS 9.23；Rolling Forcing 对应为 78.63、80.05、82.20、68.92、5.32、7.95。验证器接受 32.1% 的提议（每视频 28 轮中 9 轮），带来 1.20× 加速；不做验证直接提交 G1/G2 预测的加速为 1.56× 和 1.89×，但漂移升至 4.22 和 4.51。消融显示，预测偏移 {1} 时 Quality 81.00、漂移 4.08，{1,2} 为 81.29/3.29，扩到 {1,2,4} 漂移降到 2.89 但 Quality 跌至 80.21。
article.why_it_matters: 它把「预测更远的未来」当作训练时的表示学习目标，而不是推理期的补丁，为长视频一致性提供了与噪声调度、KV 缓存管理正交的一条路。预测头还能复用为投机式采样，兼顾质量与速度。
article.limitations: 每个提交的块仍需一次无法跳过的 cache-update pass（约占标准推理时间 20%），加速因此远低于跳过窗口的比例。理论分析限于 W=1、精确对齐 α=0，且作者明确表示未把可辨识性与漂移形式化关联；LongLive 的漂移 3.43 和 VideoScore 3.108 仍略优于本文的 3.64 和 3.069。
article.figure_caption_zh: 左：窗口内联合去噪 5 个块后，2 个预测头从最后一块特征并行预测第 6、7 块，前端的干净块被提交、窗口前移；右：为下一块生成 3 个候选，由验证器选出一个或全部拒绝。

page_papers.title: Q-Learning with Scalar Adjoint Matching
page_papers.abstract: Flow policies capture rich and diverse action distributions, and fine-tuning them with off-policy RL to improve beyond the demonstrations has drawn growing interest. However, fine-tuning a flow policy against a learned value function is not trivial, because the policy generates its action over many flow steps. Adjoint matching offers a principled way to update the flow model itself by propagating value information from the final action back to each flow step, but it requires a vector--Jacobian product through the policy at every step, a cost that grows with the number of flow steps and the policy size. We observe that the batch-averaged velocity Jacobian of pretrained flow policies concentrates on its diagonal. Motivated by this finding, we derive a closed-form scalar adjoint that scales the value gradient at the final action by the flow time, eliminating the per-step vector--Jacobian products. We further find that controlling the critic's value at policy-generated actions is particularly important under the scalar adjoint. Based on these findings, we propose Q-learning with Scalar Adjoint Matching (SQAM), which combines the scalar adjoint with a value penalty at those actions. SQAM's gains concentrate on the four hardest OGBench domains, where its success rate exceeds that of the strongest baseline in each domain by 18 to 35 percentage points. To test whether SQAM extends to large pretrained policies, we also fine-tune a vision-language-action policy on a real bimanual robot. SQAM improves over supervised fine-tuning on all three tasks.

Abstract
Flow policies capture rich and diverse action distributions, and fine-tuning them with off-policy RL to improve beyond the demonstrations has drawn growing interest. However, fine-tuning a flow policy against a learned value function is not trivial, because the policy generates its action over many flow steps. Adjoint matching offers a principled way to update the flow model itself by propagating value information from the final action back to each flow step, but it requires a vector–Jacobian product through the policy at every step, a cost that grows with the number of flow steps and the policy size. We observe that the batch-averaged velocity Jacobian of pretrained flow policies concentrates on its diagonal. Motivated by this finding, we derive a closed-form scalar adjoint that scales the value gradient at the final action by the flow time, eliminating the per-step vector–Jacobian products. We further find that controlling the critic’s value at policy-generated actions is particularly important under the scalar adjoint. Based on these findings, we propose Q-learning with Scalar Adjoint Matching (SQAM), which combines the scalar adjoint with a value penalty at those actions. SQAM’s gains concentrate on the four hardest OGBench domains, where its success rate exceeds that of the strongest baseline in each domain by 18 to 35 percentage points. To test whether SQAM extends to large pretrained policies, we also fine-tune a vision-language-action policy on a real bimanual robot. SQAM improves over supervised fine-tuning on all three tasks.

1
Introduction
Flow policies represent rich and multimodal action distributions, and they have become a common
policy class for offline and offline-to-online RL
(
Park et al., 2025b
;
Li and Levine, 2026
;
Dong et al., 2026c
;
Chi et al., 2023
)
as well as the backbone of recent large pretrained robot policies
(
Intelligence et al., 2025b
;
Bjorck et al., 2025
)
.
Improving such a policy beyond the data it was trained on calls for fine-tuning it with off-policy RL
against a learned action-value function
(
Intelligence et al., 2025a
;
Wang et al., 2026
;
Dong et al., 2026a
;
Xu et al., 2026
;
Li et al., 2025b
;
Chen et al., 2025
)
.
However, fine-tuning a flow policy to maximize a learned value function is not a trivial problem because of its multiple sampling procedure
(
Park et al., 2025b
;
Zhang et al., 2026
)
. Most methods therefore freeze the policy and work outside it, adding a separately learned residual to the actions it produces
(
Dong et al., 2026b
;
Xiao et al., 2026
)
or learning with RL which input noise to feed the frozen policy
(
Wagenmaker et al., 2025
)
, which leaves the pretrained policy intact during training. The improvement then rests on a separately learned component rather than on the generative model itself, so it is either bounded by what the frozen policy can express or forfeits the expressiveness of the flow policy. On the other hand, adjoint matching
(
Domingo-Enrich et al., 2025
;
Li and Levine, 2026
;
Dong et al., 2026c
)
provides a theoretically grounded alternative for directly updating the flow model with value functions. It propagates value information from the final action back to each flow step to guide the model’s updates. However, this requires a vector–Jacobian product through the policy at every step, so the computational cost grows with the number of flow steps and policy size.
In this work, we observe that the batch-averaged velocity Jacobian of a pretrained flow policy concentrates on its diagonal (
Figure
2
). This suggests that the vector–Jacobian product adjoint matching
pays for at every flow step may not be necessary. Inspired by this finding, we approximate the
Jacobian by a scalar multiple of the identity, under which the propagation admits a closed form that
scales the value gradient at the final action by the flow time (
Proposition
1
). We call this
the scalar adjoint. It needs a single critic gradient at the sampled action and no vector–Jacobian
product through the policy, and
Section
4.2
shows that it preserves the qualitative trends
of the exact propagation.
We further find that the effectiveness of the scalar adjoint depends on the value-learning scheme. We investigate this dependence and identify the critic’s value at policy-generated actions as particularly important. Our regularization ablations isolate this dependency. Methods that regulate the
critic at these actions improve performance, while methods that act only on dataset
(
Kostrikov et al., 2022
)
or action distance
(
Tarasov et al., 2023
)
provide little improvement
(
Section
4.3
). Based on these findings, we propose
Q-learning with Scalar Adjoint Matching
(SQAM), which combines the scalar adjoint with a value penalty at policy-generated actions.
Through experiments on the
50
50
OGBench
(
Park et al., 2025a
)
tasks, SQAM outperforms prior methods in both offline RL and offline-to-online RL, and the gains concentrate where the benchmark is hardest. On the four hardest domains it adds
18
18
to
35
35
percentage points of offline success rate over the best
baseline in each, and it reaches
75
%
75\%
against
68
%
68\%
for the strongest baseline overall. To assess whether SQAM extends to large pretrained policies, we apply it to offline-to-online RL fine-tuning of a vision-language-action model
(
Kim et al., 2026b
)
on a real-world bimanual robot
(
Rainbow Robotics, 2024
)
equipped with two
20

(
Wuji Technology, 2025
)
. We observe that SQAM clearly improves over supervised fine-tuning on all three manipulation tasks, while residual fine-tuning
(
Dong et al., 2026a
)
struggles in the same setting.

Figure

adjoints contract in the same way as the flow time approaches zero, so the regression target in

3.2

the scalar adjoint relies directly on the critic’s gradient, this correspondence led us to examine the
role of the value learning scheme in this framework, which
Section
4.3
presents.

5
Related work
Propagating value to intermediate flow steps.
A flow policy generates its action over many flow
steps, while the critic evaluates only the final action. Using the critic to steer the flow therefore requires propagating its value to each intermediate step, and existing methods differ mainly in how they do
so
(
Lee et al., 2026
)
. The most common approach evaluates the critic at a
Tweedie posterior estimate of the final action, and it is used for guidance at test
time
(
Chung et al., 2023
;
Kim et al., 2025
;
Zhou et al., 2026
)
.
Another line avoids the approximation and feeds the intermediate action to the critic directly, either
by matching the policy’s score to the critic’s action gradient at the intermediate
action
(
Psenka et al., 2024
)
or by learning a separate value at each noise
level
(
Oberai et al., 2026
;
Doo et al., 2026
)
. Adjoint
matching
(
Domingo-Enrich et al., 2025
;
Li and Levine, 2026
;
Dong et al., 2026c
;
Bergmeister et al., 2026
)
gives a theoretically
grounded answer, propagating the value gradient back to each flow step through the lean adjoint ODE.
For test-time guidance rather than fine-tuning, dropping the Jacobian has also been found to outperform
backpropagating through the exact Jacobian
(
Zhou et al., 2026
)
.
Critic regularization.
Many value learning schemes regularize the critic, and they differ
in where the regularization acts. CQL penalizes the critic’s value at the actions the policy prefers relative to the data
(
Kumar et al., 2020
)
, IQL fits a state value by expectile regression and trains the critic by TD regression toward it, using only dataset actions
(
Kostrikov et al., 2022
)
, and ReBRAC subtracts an action-distance penalty from the bootstrap target
(
Tarasov et al., 2023
)
. Fisher-BRC penalizes the action
gradient of the critic’s offset from a behavior model
(
Kostrikov et al., 2021
)
, which is close to the gradient-norm penalty we compare in
Section
4.3
, and Cal-QL calibrates the critic against a reference policy for offline-to-online fine-tuning
(
Nakamoto et al., 2023
)
.
Offline-to-online RL.
Pretraining a policy and a critic on offline data and then fine-tuning
them online is a standard recipe for sample-efficient
RL
(
Ball et al., 2023
;
Hester et al., 2018
;
Hu et al., 2024
;
Kostrikov et al., 2022
;
Kumar et al., 2020
;
Lei et al., 2024
;
Luo et al., 2024
;
Nair et al., 2021
;
Nakamoto et al., 2023
;
Rajeswaran et al., 2018
;
Vecerik et al., 2018
)
.
A central challenge is the distribution shift at the transition, which destabilizes the value
function and can make the policy forget what it learned
offline
(
Ball et al., 2023
;
Nakamoto et al., 2023
;
Wołczyk et al., 2024
)
.
6
Conclusion
We introduced SQAM, which fine-tunes flow policies with off-policy RL without a vector–Jacobian
product through the policy. Motivated by the diagonal structure of the batch-averaged velocity
Jacobian, it replaces the exact adjoint with a closed-form scalar adjoint and pairs it with a value
penalty at the policy-generated actions. SQAM improves most on the four hardest OGBench domains
and extends to a vision-language-action policy on a real robot.
Our results also suggest a broader point. A rough approximation of the adjoint suffices, while the
value learning scheme largely determines how well it performs. The bottleneck of
off-policy RL with flow policies may therefore lie less in the policy update than in the critic. We
hope this encourages further work on value learning for flow policies.

Ethics statement
This work fine-tunes robot policies with reinforcement learning in simulation and on a robot in a
controlled laboratory setting. The real-robot experiments involve no human subjects and no personal
data, and an operator supervised the robot throughout. As with any method that improves a policy
against a learned value function, deployment beyond a supervised setting calls for the usual
safeguards.

We used generative AI tools to assist with writing, editing, and routine coding and plotting. We did
not use them to generate research ideas, experimental results, or claims. The authors reviewed all

Appendix E
Real-robot experiments: RB-Y1 with Wuji Hand 2
This appendix documents the real-robot experiments on a dual-arm RB-Y1
humanoid
(
Rainbow Robotics, 2024
)
equipped with two Wuji Hand 2 dexterous hands
(
Wuji Technology, 2025
)
. For
each of three manipulation tasks we follow the same pipeline: (i) behavior cloning (BC) of a
vision-language-action base policy on teleoperated demonstrations, (ii) collection of 30 rollout
episodes of the BC policy on the robot, (iii) offline RL for 15K steps on the demonstrations plus these
30 BC rollout episodes, (iv) online RL for a further 10K steps that continues from the offline
checkpoint while the robot collects new episodes, and (v) a 30-episode evaluation of every checkpoint.
The same protocol is run for our method (SQAM) and for the EXPO-FT
baseline
(
Dong et al., 2026a
)
.
E.1
Platform, observations and actions
Figure 9
:
Hardware setup: RB-Y1 humanoid with a Wuji Hand 2 on each wrist
and a head-mounted ZED Mini stereo camera.
Hardware.
We use a Rainbow Robotics RB-Y1
(
Rainbow Robotics, 2024
)
dual-arm humanoid with a 20-DoF Wuji
Hand 2
(
Wuji Technology, 2025
)
mounted on each wrist. The experiments use 54 of its degrees of freedom, the two 7-DoF arms and the
two 20-DoF hands, for bimanual tabletop manipulation. The torso and neck stay at fixed joint positions, and
the mobile base is not used. A single Stereolabs ZED Mini stereo camera
(
Stereolabs, 2018
)
mounted on the
head provides the visual input (
Figure
9
).
Observation space.
At every policy query the observation has three parts. The first is two ego-centric RGB images, the
left and right views of the ZED Mini stereo pair, captured at 30 Hz and resized to
192
×
320
192\times 320
. The
second is a 62-dimensional proprioceptive vector of measured joint positions. The third is the task instruction
(
Table
6
).
Action space.
Actions are absolute joint-position targets. The base policy predicts an action chunk of 24 steps, and
its first 16 steps are executed. RL acts only on these
16
16
executed steps and on the 54 arm and
hand joints. SQAM optimizes this sub-chunk by
updating the action head of the base policy, whereas EXPO-FT keeps the base policy frozen and adds a
residual to it through its edit policy.
Control loop.
The robot runs at a nominal control rate of 30 Hz and executes the policy synchronously. At each
policy query the current observation is sent to the actor and the returned 16 step chunk of
joint-position targets is executed step by step. A new observation is taken and the next chunk is
requested only after the chunk has been completed.

Appendix H
Limitations and future work
We see three directions that this work leaves open.
Value learning for flow policies.
Our results suggest that the value learning scheme largely
determines how well the scalar adjoint performs, and SQAM addresses this with a value penalty added
to a standard critic. A value learning method designed for flow policies from the ground up may make
this dependence more reliable than a penalty on top of an existing critic.
Multi-task fine-tuning.
Updating the generative policy itself, rather than a separately
learned component, should matter most when a single policy serves many tasks. Our real-robot experiments
fine-tune the policy on each task separately. Fine-tuning a single policy across many tasks, as in
Wang et al. (2026)
, would test this benefit more directly.
Why the Jacobian concentrates on its diagonal.
We observe that the batch-averaged velocity
Jacobian of pretrained flow policies concentrates on its diagonal on every domain we measured, but we
do not explain why. A theoretical analysis of when this structure arises would clarify the conditions
under which the scalar adjoint applies.

article.headline: 跳过逐点VJP，flow策略RL微调更省算力
article.lede: 预训练flow策略的速度雅可比近似对角，作者据此推出闭式标量伴随，省去每步VJP；最难四域成功率提升18–35点。
article.problem: 用off-policy RL把flow策略微调到演示数据之上时，策略要在多步采样链上生成动作，而critic只评价最终动作。adjoint matching能把价值梯度回传到每个flow步，但每一步都要过一遍向量–雅可比积，其开销随flow步数与策略规模增长，难以支撑越来越大的预训练策略。
article.method: 作者发现，预训练flow策略的批平均速度雅可比集中在对角线上，于是把雅可比近似为标量乘单位阵，推导出闭式解：每个flow步的伴随向量就是最终动作处critic梯度的−τ倍，只需一次梯度、不做过VJP。作者进一步指出标量伴随直接依赖策略生成动作处的critic梯度，因而在critic损失中加入该动作与数据集动作的价值差惩罚（value penalty），与标量伴随合起来构成SQAM。
article.results: 在OGBench全部50个任务上，SQAM离线训练1M步的平均成功率为75%，最强基线TRQAM为68%；增益集中在四个最难域，分别比各域最强基线高21、18、22、35个百分点，cube-quadruple上由19%提升到54%。真机上微调视觉-语言-动作策略RLDX-1，三个任务各评测30条episode：SFT为15/30、7/30、4/30，SQAM离线转在线后为25/30、15/30、13/30，而EXPO-FT在该设置下表现不佳。
article.why_it_matters: 它把flow策略的RL微调成本从「每步一次VJP」降到「一次critic梯度」，在策略规模增大时更容易扩展，并在真机VLA策略上显示出超过监督微调的效果。作者据此提出，当前瓶颈可能不在策略更新而在critic的价值学习。
article.limitations: 雅可比近似对角只是跨10个域的经验观察，作者明确表示未解释其成因；标量伴随与精确伴随仍有夹角，在操作类域上更大，正是单用标量伴随表现较差的域，而value penalty在cube-double上因降低离线性能被关闭。真机实验只覆盖3个任务、每任务30条评测episode、固定初始配置且按任务分别微调，多任务场景尚未验证。

page_papers.title: Disentangling Dual Image References in Frequency Aware Diffusion Models for Personalized Generation
page_papers.abstract: Personalized image generation aims to synthesize text-driven images conditioned on reference images, while mainly casting the generation as image customization for foreground and style transfer for background. Previous arts of diffusion models suffers from the text misalignment with background for image customization and foreground for style transfer during the denoising process. Such facts, as we observed, rooted from the entanglement among hybrid frequency bands during the denoising process. To address such salient limitation, in this paper, we study personalized generation based on dual references - customization and color and style reference - and propose a paradigm to disentangle these Dual image references within Frequency-aware Diffusion Models, dubbed Dual-FDM, to simultaneously tackle two crucial personalized image generation tasks: customization style transfer and color style transfer, by disentangling different frequency bands via mask strategy within frequency domain. For customization style transfer, we replace the mid-frequency band of the background in the style reference with that from the foreground of the customized reference. For color style transfer, we substitute the low-frequency band of the background in the style reference with that from both the foreground and background of the color reference. Both the substituted frequency bands are used as the key and value to reconstruct the query foreground and background of the denoised personalized image.Extensive experiments validate the superiority of Dual-FDM over the state-of-the-art diffusion models for personalized image generation. Our code can be accessed from https://github.com/htyjers/Dual-FDM.
page_papers.content:
Disentangling Dual Image References in Frequency Aware Diffusion Models for Personalized Generation
Haipeng Liu
Yang Wang
†
†
thanks:
Yang Wang is the corresponding author
Meng Wang
Affiliation:
School of Computer Science and Information Engineering
Affiliation:
Hefei University of Technology, China
Email:
hpliu_hfut@hotmail.com
yangwang@hfut.edu.cn
eric.mengwang@gmail.com
Abstract
Personalized image generation aims to synthesize text-driven images conditioned on reference images, while mainly casting the generation as image customization for foreground and style transfer for background. Previous arts of diffusion models suffers from the text misalignment with background for image customization and foreground for style transfer during the denoising process. Such facts, as we observed, rooted from the entanglement among hybrid frequency bands during the denoising process. In particular, the low-frequency band primarily captures color information, mid-frequency band encodes global structure, while high-frequency band corresponds to local texture.
Besides, the early (high-noise) denoising stage mainly focuses on the low-and-mid frequency bands, while the late (low-noise) denoising stage progressively exhibits the high-frequency band, resulting in the dominance of low-and-mid over high frequency bands, especially when entangled within a single image reference, tends to reinforce each other at the early stage, hence the pitfall of overwhelming suppression of text prompt guidance. To address such salient limitation, in this paper, we study personalized generation based on dual references - customization and color and style reference - and propose a paradigm to disentangle these
Dual
image references within
F
requency-aware
D
iffusion
M
odels, dubbed
Dual-FDM
, to simultaneously tackle two crucial personalized image generation tasks: customization style transfer and color style transfer, by disentangling different frequency bands via mask strategy within frequency domain. For customization style transfer, we replace the mid-frequency band of the background in the style reference with that from the foreground of the customized reference. For color style transfer, we substitute the low-frequency band of the background in the style reference with that from both the foreground and background of the color reference. Both the substituted frequency bands are used as the key and value to reconstruct the query foreground and background of the denoised personalized image.
We further compute the ratio of information entropy of the substituted frequency bands to adaptively modulate the denoising timesteps between the early and late stages. Extensive experiments validate the superiority of
Dual-FDM
over the state-of-the-art diffusion models for personalized image generation. Our code can be accessed from
https://github.com/htyjers/Dual-FDM
.
Figure 1
:
Personalized images generated by our
Dual-FDM
. (a) The generated examples of
Dual-FDM
cust
for customized references (left) and style references (above); (b) The generated examples of
Dual-FDM

for color references (left) and style references (above).
1
Introduction
Figure 2
:
(a) Comparison of the generated results, as well as the attention score map of text prompts and image references, between IP-Adapter
Ye et al. (2023)
and MS-Diffusion
Wang et al. (2025)
for image customization. (b) Comparison of the generated results between InstantStyle
Wang et al. (2024a)
and StyleStudio
Lei et al. (2025)
for style transfer. (c) Comparison of generated results guided by different frequency band of the image reference.
Personalized image generation focuses on synthesizing text-driven images conditioned on reference images, which enjoys remarkable progress, benefiting from the powerful denosing capabilities of Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (DDPMs)
Ho et al. (2020)
;
Liu et al. (2024)
;
Liu et al. (2025a)
,
e.g.
, Stable Diffusion
Rombach et al. (2022)
;
Esser et al. (2024)
;
Podell et al. (2023)
;
Qian et al. (2022)
;
Qian et al. (2023)
;
Wang et al. (2024c)
. Typically, the personalized image generation involves two key subtasks,
i.e.
,
image customization
and
style transfer
. Given text prompts, image customization
Xiao et al. (2025)
;
Zeng et al. (2024)
;
Pang et al. (2024)
;
Gal et al. (2022)
;
Ruiz et al. (2023)
;
Kumari et al. (2023)
;
Liu et al. (2025b)
;
Ma et al. (2024)
;
Li et al. (2024)
;
Li et al. (2023)
;
Liu et al. (2022)
;
Cao et al. (2026)
;
Jiang et al. (2026)
aims to generate images by substituting the foreground semantics in the text prompts with the foreground extracted from the reference images, while preserving the background of the text prompts. In contrast, style transfer
Qin et al. (2025)
;
Rout et al. (2025)
;
Liu et al. (2023)
;
Sohn et al. (2023)
;
Zhu et al. (2025)
;
Qi et al. (2024)
;
Hertz et al. (2024)
;
Lei et al. (2025)
;
Gao et al. (2024)
;
Xing et al. (2024)
;
Wang et al. (2024b)
;
Wang et al. (2024a)
;
Jeong et al. (2024)
;
Wang et al. (2022)
focuses on disentangling style (
background
) from reference images and aligning the foreground with the text prompt. However, prior arts have struggled to align the generated image with the text prompts within each individual subtask.
Figure 3
:
Illustration of our proposed
Dual-FDM
pipeline (a); For customization style transfer (b), we replace the mid-frequency band of the background in the style reference with that from the foreground of the customized reference, named
Dual-FDM
cust
(Sec.
2.3
). For the color style transfer (c), we substitute the low-frequency band of the background in the style reference with that from both the foreground and background of the color reference, named
Dual-FDM
cost
(Sec.
2.4
). Each of the two personalized image generation tasks are conducted in the early and late stage of the whole denoising process guided by text prompts as illustrated in Eq. (
1
).
For image customization, substantial efforts
Ye et al. (2023)
;
Aiello et al. (2025)
;
Huang et al. (2025b)
aim to
emphasize dense image references of the foreground while overwhelming sparse text prompts of the background, especially for complex ones
,
e.g.
, a degraded “
flower wreath
” and the missing “
coffee
” in the IP-Adapter
Ye et al. (2023)
of Fig.
2
(a). Building on this, layout-based methods
Wang et al. (2025)
;
Huang et al. (2025b)
;
Zhang et al. (2024)
exploit spatial layouts to explicitly constrain reference concepts to the foreground, while assigning background regions to text prompts.
This preserves the foreground identity, but the explicit separation of foreground and background in the layout disrupts overall consistency, leading to the misalignment with (complex / long) text prompts.
As illustrated in the MS-Diffusion
Wang et al. (2025)
of Fig.
2
(a), the generated spatial arrangement of “
flower wreath
” and “
coffee
” diverges from the prompt and instead resembles
“A flower wreath around a dog near a coffee”
.
When coming to style transfer, during the early stage of the denoising process with high-level noise, the foreground is reconstructed from sparse text prompts,
the dense style information intended for the background often leaks into the foreground, resulting in misalignment with the text prompts
,
e.g.
, the incorrect number of “
woman
" in the InstantStyle
Wang et al. (2024a)
of Fig.
2
(b). To resolve such issue, StyleStudio
Lei et al. (2025)
applies style via instance normalization
Huang and Belongie (2017)
in the cross-attention layers and leverages layout to preserve foreground in the self-attention layers. Nevertheless, self-attention score maps highlight only the most salient regions, implying that the extracted layout can align only with simple text prompts (
i.e.
, “
a dog
") rather than the multi-objects (“
two pillows and one lemon
" in the StyleStudio
Lei et al. (2025)
of Fig.
2
(b)) text prompts, thereby
preventing it from handling the complex text prompts
.
So far, neither image customization nor style transfer achieves satisfactory alignment between the generated image and the text prompt for diffusion models. Such facts, as we observed, rooted from the entanglement among hybrid frequency bands. Intuitively, as shown in Fig.
2
(c), the low-frequency and mid-frequency bands capture color and global structure, while high-frequency band focuses on local texture, where different frequency bands are mainly denoised during
different
stages of the denoising process. As we observed, the early (high-noise) denoising stage mainly focuses on the low-and-mid frequency bands, while the late (low-noise) denoising stage progressively exhibits the high-frequency band (See Sec.
A
of the Appendix), the dominance of low-and-mid over high frequency bands, especially when entangled within a single image reference, suggesting reinforce each other at the early stages, resulting in an overwhelming suppression of text prompt guidance.
To resolve the text misalignment for personalization generation, we propose to solve the problem upon dual references and develop a paradigm to disentangle these
Dual
image references within
F
requency-aware
D
iffusion
M
odels, dubbed
Dual-FDM
, for two classical personalized image generation tasks in a row: customization style transfer and color style transfer, by disentangling different frequency bands via mask strategy within frequency domain. Specifically:
•
We propose to map the foreground or background of image references into the frequency domain via Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT), where a mask is applied from left to right to progressively disentangle the low-, mid-, and high-frequency bands. Notably, for customization style transfer, we replace the mid-frequency band of the background in the style reference with that from the foreground of the customized reference, named
Dual-FDM
cust
(Fig.
1
(a)). The style reference with the mid-frequency band substituted is used as the key and value to reconstruct the query foreground and background of the denoised personalized image in the decoupled cross-attention layer. For the color style transfer, we substitute the low-frequency band of the background in the style reference with that from both the foreground and background of the color reference, named

cost

1
(b)). The style reference with the substituted low-frequency band is further utilized as the key and value to reconstruct the query foreground and background of the denoised personalized image in the decoupled cross-attention layer.
•
To pop up the foreground or background of the image reference, we utilize the key projection matrices in the decoupled cross-attention layer to represent the foreground, which are then reformulated through singular value decomposition (SVD) to derive the corresponding
background matrix
for the background.
•
For each task, we further compute the ratio of information entropy of the substituted frequency bands to adaptively modulate the denoising timesteps between the early and late stages, so as to achieve a well-balanced performance between text alignment and dual-image similarity.
Extensive experiments validate the superiority of Dual-FDM over the state-of-the-art diffusion models for personalized image generation.

); 3) how to disentangle the low-frequency band in color style transfer (Sec.
2.4
); 4) how to adaptively modulate the timesteps within the denoising process between early and late stages (Sec.
2.5
). Before shedding light on Dual-FDM, we elaborate the preliminary regarding decoupled cross-attention mechanism, which plays a pivotal role of personalized image generation.

Conclusion
In this paper, we study personalized generation based on dual references - customization and color and style reference - and propose a paradigm to disentangle dual image references within frequency-aware diffusion models, dubbed
Dual-FDM
, for two classical personalized image generation tasks in a row: customization style transfer and color style transfer, by disentangling different frequency bands via mask strategy within frequency domain. Extensive experiments validate
the superiority of
Dual-FDM
over the state-of-the-art diffusion models.

Appendix A
Frequency Variation During the Denoising Process
As mentioned in Sec.
1
of the mainbody, We claim that
during the denoising process, images recover low-and-mid frequency bands first, followed by high-frequency details
. To validate the claims via frequency analysis, we experimentally measure the changes in both low- and high-frequency bands at different timesteps during the denoising process. The results are reported in Tab.
5
:
•
Low-frequency information.
We adopt
Mean Gray
,
Mean HSV-V
, and
Mean Luma
, which primarily capture global brightness and luminance structure. These metrics quantify the stability of the low-frequency bands throughout the denoising process.
•
High-frequency information.
We use
Average Gradient
,
Variance
, and
LBP Variance
, which are sensitive to edge sharpness, local contrast, and texture complexity. These metrics reflect the recovery of high-frequency details.
The low-frequency metrics remain nearly unchanged from the beginning (e.g.,
Mean Gray varies only slightly from 119.5 to 120.9

Appendix C
The algorithm of customization style transfer and color style transfer
Due to the page limitation, we summarize the process of customization style transfer in Algorithm
1
and color style transfer in Algorithm
2
.
To tackle the text-alignment issue in personalized image generation, in this paper, we study personalized generation based on dual references - customization and color and style reference - and propose a paradigm to disentangle these
Dual
image references within
F
requency-aware
D
iffusion
M
odels, dubbed
Dual-FDM
, for two classical personalized image generation tasks in a row: customization style transfer and color style transfer, by disentangling different frequency bands via mask strategy within frequency domain. For customization style transfer, we replace the mid-frequency band of the background in the style reference with that from the foreground of the customized reference. For color style transfer, we substitute the low-frequency band of the background in the style reference with that from both the foreground and background of the color reference. Both the substituted frequency bands are used as the key and value to reconstruct the query foreground and background of the denoised personalized image.
For each task, we further compute the ratio of information entropy of the substituted frequency bands to adaptively modulate the denoising timesteps between the early and late stages.

Datasets.
We evaluate

on combined datasets covering image customization, style transfer, and text-to-image (T2I) generation:

Image Customization

+

Peng et al. (2025)
: the latest human-aligned personalized image generation benchmark, comprising 65 object classes, 20 human classes, and 45 animal classes. For each image, 9 text prompts are generated by GPT-4o to span a range of difficulty levels.

: 1)

Gao et al. (2024)

•
T2I generation
:
T2I-CompBench++
Huang et al. (2025a)
: an enhanced benchmark for compositional text-to-image generation. T2I-CompBench++ comprises 8,000 compositional text prompts categorized into four primary groups: attribute binding, object relationships, generative numeracy, and complex compositions. These are further divided into eight sub-categories.
Based on the above, we construct several combined datasets for different joint tasks: 1) for customization style transfer (small-scale), we concatenate
DreamBench
and

DreamBench++
as the customization references and

as the style references; 3) for color style transfer, we combine

and

as the color and style references, while text prompts are provided by

for stylized image generation.
Metrics.
We consider 9 evaluation metrics from three aspects to evaluate our
Dual-FDM
:
•
Text and Image Reference Alignment
: we follow previous methods and adopt two representative models,
CLIP
2
2
2
Since CLIP is trained on real image–text (T) pairs, it is particularly sensitive to image style, which may distort text–image similarity. To alleviate this, we propose CLIP-TS by measuring similarity with style reference (S), thereby reducing the style influence . In addition, the generated background aligned with text prompts can interfere with the customized reference (C); hence we propose CLIP-TC, which incorporates text prompts to suppress such interference. We also provide CLIP-T (image–text similarity) and CLIP-CS (image–image reference similarity) for comparison.
and
DINO
Caron et al. (2021)
, for evaluation. Specifically,
CLIP-T
measures the similarity between generated images and the given text prompts;
CLIP-TC
and
CLIP-TS
evaluate the similarity between generated images and customized (or style) reference images while jointly considering the text prompts; finally,
CLIP-CS
assesses the similarity between generated images and dual-reference images.

Image Generation Quality

Xu et al. (2023)
to model human preferences for image quality and
HPS V2
Wu et al. (2023)
that combines perceptual studies with deep learning for comprehensive visual and semantic assessment. Both metrics measure the semantics consistency of the high-quality image generation aligned with human standards;

Times

article.headline: 频域掩码解耦双参考图，统一个性化生成
article.lede: 合肥工业大学团队提出 Dual-FDM，在频域用掩码分离两张参考图的不同频段，同时处理定制风格迁移与颜色风格迁移。
article.problem: 个性化图像生成包含图像定制与风格迁移两类子任务，但已有扩散模型常出现生成结果与文本提示不对齐：定制时背景被图像参考淹没，风格迁移时风格信息泄漏到前景。作者将根源归因于去噪过程中混合频段的纠缠——低频携带颜色、中频编码全局结构、高频对应局部纹理，而早期高噪声阶段主要恢复低中频，当其纠缠在单张图像参考中时会相互强化，压制文本提示的引导。
article.method: Dual-FDM 先用离散余弦变换（DCT）把参考图的前景或背景映射到频域，用从左到右的掩码切出低、中、高频带；同时对解耦交叉注意力中的 key 投影矩阵做奇异值分解并取奇异值倒数，构造“背景矩阵”以压制前景、增强背景。定制风格迁移把风格参考背景的中频替换为定制参考前景的中频，颜色风格迁移则把风格参考背景的低频替换为颜色参考前景与背景的低频，替换后的频带作为 key 和 value 重建去噪图像的前景与背景。最后用替换频带的信息熵比值自适应划分早期与晚期去噪步数。
article.results: 在 DreamBench/TI 与 DreamBench++ 等组合数据上，Dual-FDM_cust 取得 CLIP-T 0.3194、CLIP-TC 0.5031、CLIP-CS 0.6687、IR 5.3487、HPS 2.6007；相比 MS-Diffusion+CSGO，在 CLIP-T 上最多领先 2.27%、CLIP-TC 7.5%、CLIP-CS 4.17%、DINO-CS 27.28%、HPS 2.24%。颜色风格迁移在 T2I-CompBench++ 的 Color 类别上取得 CLIP-TS 0.5015、CLIP-S 0.7178、DINO-S 0.4970。单张推理耗时 10.26 秒、显存 12.48GB，在表 10 的对比方法中为最低。实验基于 IP-Adapter 与 SDXL、30 步采样、单张 RTX 4090。
article.why_it_matters: 它提供了一个无需额外训练、以频域解耦统一“定制”与“颜色或风格”两类参考的视角，且推理开销低于多数对比方法，对个性化生成的可控性研究有直接参考价值。
article.limitations: 作者在附录中承认，当风格参考只包含极稀疏图案（如线条结构）时，中频定制线索会衰减高频风格细节，导致风格信息不完整。此外论文检查表标注未做误差棒或统计显著性检验，结论的稳健性仍待验证。

page_papers.title: DiffusionRVGE: Reinforcement Learning via Regression-Based Value Gradient Estimation
page_papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning improves diffusion models using rewards on generated images, but repeated denoising and gradient estimation make training expensive. We introduce \method, an efficient method that constructs useful update directions by regressing centered rewards on centered final denoised images. It requires neither reward derivatives nor adjoint backpropagation through the sampling trajectory. A unified first-variation formulation identifies the value-gradient target with or without a trajectory-KL penalty. A population analysis under Gaussian noising explains the regression geometry, while a subspace analysis motivates clean-image coordinates. The implementation adapts rollout bandwidth and query weights to reward continuity: local rollouts suit smooth rewards, whereas broader groups provide informative contrasts for discrete rewards. Trained jointly on five rewards, one SD3.5-Medium model matches or exceeds DiffusionNFT's joint model on seven of eight metrics, reaching GenEval $0.94$, OCR $0.92$, and PickScore $23.82$ at about one fifth of its estimated training compute. In single-reward training, \method reaches matched reward thresholds $2.1$--$6.7\times$ faster than reproduced DiffusionNFT on identical hardware. Ablations support the clean-image estimator, direct direction transfer, and reward-dependent rollout choices. Code is available at https://github.com/jy-wang-tsinghua/DIFFUSIONRVGE.

Abstract
Reinforcement learning improves diffusion models using rewards on generated images, but repeated denoising and gradient estimation make training expensive. We introduce DiffusionRVGE, an efficient method that constructs useful update directions by regressing centered rewards on centered final denoised images. It requires neither reward derivatives nor adjoint backpropagation through the sampling trajectory. A unified first-variation formulation identifies the value-gradient target with or without a trajectory-KL penalty. A population analysis under Gaussian noising explains the regression geometry, while a subspace analysis motivates clean-image coordinates. The implementation adapts rollout bandwidth and query weights to reward continuity: local rollouts suit smooth rewards, whereas broader groups provide informative contrasts for discrete rewards. Trained jointly on five rewards, one SD3.5-Medium model matches or exceeds DiffusionNFT’s joint model on seven of eight metrics, reaching GenEval

Introduction
Diffusion and flow matching models generate images by transforming noise into data
(
Ho et al., 2020
;
Song et al., 2021
;

;

;
Liu et al., 2025
;
Zheng et al., 2026
)

Our estimator fits centered reward differences to clean-image contrasts using normalized ridge regression. Under exact conditioning in the Gaussian noising model, the population normal equations connect clean-image regression to a covariance-preconditioned value gradient. A subspace analysis characterizes how denoised coordinates improve directional estimation, and our alignment experiments demonstrate this advantage in the evaluated models. We transfer the fitted directions directly to model updates without an adjoint backward pass.
Regression uses reward values and benefits from informative variation across the rollout bank. Smooth scores permit local perturbations; discrete scores can remain constant across these perturbations and benefit from independent-seed groups. We therefore adapt rollout bandwidth and query weights to reward continuity while retaining the same centered squared-regression estimator. This gives one practical method for both continuous preferences and discrete task scores.
Our contributions are:
•
Efficient regression-based updates.
Clean-image regression constructs update directions without reward derivatives or adjoint backpropagation, guided by gradient matching and supported by directional analysis and empirical validation.
•
Reward-adaptive implementation.
Local trajectory banks and broader rollout groups share a centered regression formulation, with reward-dependent query weights validated by ablations.
•
Strong results at lower compute.
Our joint model matches or exceeds DiffusionNFT on seven of eight metrics at about one fifth of its estimated training compute. Single-reward runs reach matched thresholds

DiffusionRVGE constructs update directions by regressing reward differences on clean-image contrasts. Conclusion
DiffusionRVGE uses centered clean-image regression to construct useful RL directions without adjoint backpropagation. Gradient matching identifies the update target, while population and directional analyses motivate regression in clean-image coordinates. Reward-adaptive rollouts and weights handle continuous and discrete scores within one regression method. A joint model matches or exceeds DiffusionNFT on seven of eight metrics at about one fifth of its estimated training compute; single-reward runs reach matched thresholds

article.headline: 用回归估计价值梯度，扩散模型RL训练提速数倍
article.lede: 新方法把中心化奖励回归到干净图像上构造更新方向，跳过奖励求导与轨迹反向传播，宣称以约五分之一算力匹配或超越Diffusi
article.problem: 用强化学习微调扩散或流匹配模型时，每次更新都要完整去噪并估计模型改动对最终奖励的影响，训练成本很高。DDPO、Flow-GRPO、DiffusionNFT 等做法要么在采样轨迹上反传，要么需要奖励的导数。作者希望在显著更低的算力下拿到同样有效的更新方向。
article.method: 论文先用一阶变分给出带轨迹 KL 惩罚与不带惩罚时统一的价值梯度目标，再在 Gaussian 加噪模型下做总体分析，证明把中心化奖励对中心化干净图像做归一化岭回归，得到的是协方差预条件后的价值梯度方向，且不需要奖励导数。实现上按奖励连续性选择 rollout：平滑奖励（如 PickScore）用同一条轨迹上的小噪声轨迹库取局部对比，离散奖励（如 GenEval）用独立种子分组取更宽的对比，并配合奖励相关的查询权重。拟合出的方向直接用于策略更新，不做伴随反传。
article.results: 五奖励联合训练的单个 SD3.5-Medium 模型在 8 项指标中有 7 项不劣于或超过 DiffusionNFT 联合模型：GenEval 0.94、OCR 0.92、PickScore 23.82、ClipScore 0.303、HPSv2.1 0.339，仅 Aesthetic 略低（5.95 对 6.01），训练用 1000 次更新、404 GPU 小时；论文估计 DiffusionNFT 该模型至少需 2000 GPU 小时。单奖励设定下，达到相同奖励阈值比复现的 DiffusionNFT 快 2.1–6.7 倍（PickScore 2.1–2.6×、OCR 6.2–6.7×、GenEval 2.6–4.5×）；PickScore 达到 23.20 用 14.3 GPU 小时，FDFO 需 109.3。方向对齐消融中，干净图像回归把与数值 ODE 真实梯度的加权平均余弦从 0.009 提到 0.107（配对增益 0.098，95% 置信区间 [0.092, 0.106]）。
article.why_it_matters: 它把扩散模型 RL 的更新方向归结为一次小规模岭回归，避开了伴随反传和奖励求导这两个最贵的环节，让「用奖励后训练生成模型」的算力门槛明显下降。
article.limitations: 理论保证建立在 Gaussian 加噪、精确条件化以及理想化 Langevin 采样的额外假设上，属于局部或条件性结论；纯 OCR 训练出现明显的奖励劫持（DrawBench PickScore 20.32，低于基模的 22.34），需要额外设计质量下限来补救。此外对比中 DiffusionNFT 的联合训练算力是按官方代码在本机测速推算而非原文报告，复现基线也与公开行不完全一致；实验只覆盖 SD3.5-Medium、512×512 一种骨干。
article.figure_caption_zh: 图：与数值 ODE 真实梯度相比的 PickScore 余弦相似度，左、中为噪声态回归与直接干净图像回归，右为两者配对差值，阴影表示对提示重采样得到的 95% 置信区间。

figure.caption: PickScore cosine with the real gradient through the numerical ODE. Left and middle: noisy-state and direct clean-image regression. Right: paired clean-image-minus-noisy-state cosine. Shading denotes 95\% confidence intervals from resampling prompts.

Rethinking Pre-pretraining
Alexander SternCohere
Tim RocktäschelAI Centre, UCL
Acyr Locatelli
*
Cohere
Laura Ruis
*
MIT
Abstract
We report that allocating compute to synthetic pre-pretraining (PPT) never outperforms pure natural-language training in our compute-matched experiments. This holds across four PPT curricula (
k
k
-Dyck, neural cellular automata (NCA), declarative reference corpora, and code) and three training regimes: data-constrained, data-unconstrained, and a high token-to-parameter-ratio regime (881M parameters trained on 50B tokens). When natural language is scarce, repeated epochs over a 100M-token corpus beat every synthetic curriculum on natural-language validation loss, with no consistent downstream accuracy advantage from PPT. We find that PPT gains reported in prior work are sensitive to the weight initialization scheme. In an NCA reproduction, we recover a 5.4% perplexity improvement from PPT under the original initialization scheme. An alternative scheme improves both methods, but the no-PPT baseline more, closing the gap between them. However, when PPT receives
additional compute
rather than a share of the natural-language budget, gains persist at small natural-language budgets even with improved initialization, but disappear by 1B tokens. Finally, models forget what they learn during PPT in subsequent natural-language training; interleaving the same data throughout training prevents forgetting, but does not significantly improve natural-language performance. Our results suggest limited benefits of synthetic pre-pretraining as a distinct training stage and motivate rethinking how such data are used in language model training.
*
*

Equal contribution.
$\dagger$
$\dagger$
footnotetext:
Work done partly during a master’s at the UCL AI Centre and partly during an internship at Cohere.
1
Introduction
Rich computational structure can be learned from naturally occurring text. The benefits of scaling training on such tokens have yet to hit a ceiling, though increasingly large amounts of data are required for further improvements in performance
(
Kaplan et al., 2020
)
. By contrast, humans acquire language from far less linguistic experience
(
Warstadt et al., 2023
)
, and their reasoning abilities are largely dissociable from linguistic proficiency
(
Fedorenko et al., 2024
)
. This contrast has motivated recent work to ask whether useful linguistic and computational priors can instead be acquired from synthetic data. Beyond making language learning more sample-efficient, synthetic distributions supply effectively unlimited training data once high-quality natural language becomes scarce.
This idea is operationalized in prior work through pre-pretraining (PPT): a training phase on synthetic data that precedes conventional pretraining (PT) and is intended to produce an initialization with useful priors for learning language. Different synthetic distributions target different computational priors:
k
k
-Dyck encourages hierarchical dependency tracking
(
Hu et al., 2025
)
, neural cellular automata (NCA) expose models to latent transition rules and long-range dependencies
(
Lee et al., 2026
)
, and procedural tasks train operations such as copying, sorting, and retrieval
(
Jiang et al., 2026
)
. These approaches have reported gains in language modeling and context recall, including up to 8.6% lower perplexity for NCA, both when PPT is given additional compute on top of a fixed natural-language budget and when PPT and natural-language training share a fixed total compute budget.

Although prior work has demonstrated gains from synthetic PPT, how robust these gains are across other training configurations and regimes remains unclear. We therefore revisit synthetic PPT across a range of training regimes. We study three synthetic distributions (
k

-Dyck, NCA, and declarative reference corpora (DeclRef)), alongside code, which prior work has found can improve downstream reasoning beyond coding tasks
(
Aryabumi et al., 2025
)
.
We begin by asking whether synthetic PPT can provide useful inductive biases when it is not competing with natural-language training for compute. In this additive-compute setting, where PPT is added on top of a fixed natural-language budget, we first reproduce a prior NCA result as a positive control before testing the setting more broadly. We then ask whether PPT is worth its compute when it competes directly with natural-language training for a fixed FLOP budget. We evaluate this compute-matched condition across three regimes: a data-constrained setting, where the alternative is repeated training on the same 100M natural-language tokens; a data-unconstrained setting, which tests whether any PPT recipe remains competitive as training compute scales; and a high token-to-parameter ratio setting, which probes whether PPT becomes useful far beyond the Chinchilla-optimal frontier. Our findings are as follows:
1.
Gains from PPT are sensitive to the baseline initialization scheme.
We reproduce a previously reported NCA result under its original setup, recovering a 5.4% perplexity improvement from PPT. However, changing the token embedding initialization from
